## PDF page 110

[Open source PDF](../../../../sources/pdf/GTO/Poker-Math-Preflop-Workbook.pdf#page=110)

```text
                              CHAPTER SEVEN



                       IMPLIED ODDS


Often you will face bets or raises that offer you incorrect pot odds to con-
tinue. But instead of immediately throwing your hand into the muck, you
should consider the implied odds. Essentially, implied odds gauge how much
money you can expect to win the times your hand improves.

The formula for implied odds is this:

                            [( 1 / EQ ) * C ] - ( P + C )


Where C is how much you have to call right this moment, P is the size of the
pot after your opponent bets, and EQ is your hand’s equity vs. their betting
range. The answer is how much you need to win on future streets to offset
getting immediately incorrect pot odds. (Hint, if the resulting calculation is
negative, it means you already have correct pot odds to continue.)

But this may be too cumbersome to do at the tables.

Another method, and this is the one that I personally use, is to compare ratios.
Take a simple example where the pot is $10, and your opponent bets $10. You
are getting 2:1 pot odds on a call, but suspect you only have 25% equity.

So you would really need to be getting at least 3:1 pot odds to make this call
correct given the equity of your hand.



                                    PA G E 1 1 0
```

## PDF page 111

[Open source PDF](../../../../sources/pdf/GTO/Poker-Math-Preflop-Workbook.pdf#page=111)

```text
                         I M P L I E D O DD S : F A C I N G B E T S


The shortcut is to find the gap between the first numbers of the ratios and
multiply that by the bet you are facing. In this example, there is a gap of 1
between the 2 and 3, and if you multiply 1*$10 you see that you need to make
$10 extra dollars later in the hand to make this an acceptable call.



  getting           2 :1but need3 : 1
                                         gap
                                         of
                                          1 * $call
Whichever method you use to calculate implied odds is fine. Like everything
else in this workbook, the more you practice doing these calculations, the
easier it will be to make proper estimations at the table.

TOOLS TO USE: Seasoned players should be able to do this off the top of their
heads. If you are just starting out with implied odds you can download & use
the “Implied Odds” spreadsheet at www.splitsuit.pro/sheets

PROCESS: Each page contains 2 examples. Read the prompt to find the esti-
mated equity of your hand and the original pot size. Then complete the table
below for the three possible bet sizes.

TAKEAWAYS: Pay attention to how many multiples of the bet you are facing
need to be earned on future streets as your equity drops.

GLGL.




                                       PA G E 1 1 1
```
